record.original_question: Let U be an open set in the plane and λU a be the harmonic measure at the point a with respect to U . Then Øksendal [616] showed that λU a is singular U with respect to area measure. Is it also true that λa is singular with respect to β-dimensional Hausdorff measure for all β > 1? The same question can be asked for the Keldysh measure µU a at a ∈ K with respect to U a compact set K. Øksendal showed that µa is singular with respect to area measure. (B. Øksendal)

evidence.quote: Let U be an open set in the plane and λU a be the harmonic measure at the point a with respect to U . Then Øksendal [616] showed that λU a is singular U with respect to area measure.
This was proved by Makarov [550] in the case where U is simply connected; and by Jones and Wolff [467] in the general case.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $U$ be an open set in the complex plane $\mathbb{C}$ and let $a \in U$. Denote by $\lambda^U_a$ the harmonic measure at $a$ with respect to $U$, defined as the probability measure on $\partial U$ such that for every bounded continuous function $f$ on $\partial U$, the Perron solution of the Dirichlet problem with boundary data $f$ evaluated at $a$ equals $\int f\,d\lambda^U_a$. For $\beta > 0$, let $\mathcal{H}^\beta$ denote the $\beta$-dimensional Hausdorff measure on $\mathbb{C}$.

It is known that $\lambda^U_a$ is singular with respect to two-dimensional Lebesgue (area) measure. Prove or disprove: for every open set $U \subset \mathbb{C}$, every $a \in U$, and every $\beta > 1$, the harmonic measure $\lambda^U_a$ is singular with respect to $\mathcal{H}^\beta$.

Equivalently: show that there exists a Borel set $E \subset \partial U$ with $\lambda^U_a(\partial U \setminus E) = 0$ and $\mathcal{H}^\beta(E) = 0$ for all $\beta > 1$.

The analogous question is to be considered for the Keldysh measure $\mu^U_a$ at $a$ with respect to a compact set $K \subset \mathbb{C}$ (with $a \in K$), in place of $\lambda^U_a$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is solved. Makarov (1985) proved that harmonic measure on simply connected domains has Hausdorff dimension exactly 1, hence is singular with respect to $\mathcal{H}^\beta$ for $\beta>1$. Jones and Wolff (1988) extended this to arbitrary planar domains, proving that harmonic measure in any plane domain is supported on a set of Hausdorff dimension at most 1, which implies singularity with respect to $\mathcal{H}^\beta$ for all $\beta>1$.

status_evidence.title: Jones–Wolff theorem
status_evidence.snippet: Jones and Wolff (1988) proved that for any plane domain for which harmonic measure is defined, it has Hausdorff dimension at most 1.
status_evidence.claim: Harmonic measure on any plane domain is supported on a set of Hausdorff dimension ≤ 1, hence singular with respect to β-Hausdorff measure for β>1.

status_evidence.title: Makarov's theorem on harmonic measure
status_evidence.snippet: Makarov (1985) proved that for a simply connected domain in the plane, harmonic measure has Hausdorff dimension 1.
status_evidence.claim: For simply connected planar domains the singularity with respect to H^β, β>1, follows from Makarov's theorem.
